assumptions: A FALSE MEASURED SENTENCE WAS SHIPPED IN THE SOURCE AND IS REWRITTEN FROM THE MEASUREMENT, NOT HEDGED. `tracked_direct`'s docstring said the outer repository's `proof/` `comes back as ../proof/...`, which the membership rule refuses for having four components. MEASURED FALSE this round on git 2.43.0: a bare `git ls-files -z` from a WARP root vendored at `sub/` of an outer repository holding proof/WARP-9999/verdict.json answers 3 records, every one under `sub`, and ZERO beginning with `../` - the outer paths are OMITTED ENTIRELY, not respelled, so the four-component rejection is NOT what keeps them out and no contributor may treat it as the guard. The `../` spelling appears only once the cwd restriction is LIFTED by a pathspec (measured: `-- ':(top)'` answers `../proof/WARP-9999/verdict.json`). The conclusion and the behaviour were right; the stated mechanism was not, and it was a LIVE TRAP: the docstring now says explicitly that `--full-name` MUST NOT BE ADDED and why, measured by adding it to a scratch copy with the substitution asserted present - the answer is respelled from the repository top, so the vendored root's own artifacts arrive as four-component paths the rule admits NONE of (member set 2 -> 0, both genuine artifacts land in `overclaimed` so the gate reds the real corpus, and tracked_under_proof 2 -> 0, which also disarms the empty-domain leg), while `proof/<id>/<name>` becomes the OUTER root's spelling, so with the cwd restriction also lifted the outer forgery is the one record the rule admits. SECOND SOURCE CORRECTION, cosmetic but a count: the empty-domain message said `%d path(s) tracked` over a list that comes from `git ls-files`, which prints ONE RECORD PER INDEX ENTRY, so a conflicted path (measured: 3 records for 1 path) would have made it say 3 paths for one. The MESSAGE is corrected, not the count, because the count is what the check reads and behaviour is unchanged: it now says `git's index carries %d entr(ies)`, and both the owner's docstring and the divergence key say ENTRIES, NOT DISTINCT PATHS.

THE ONE ENUMERATION IS AN ENUMERATION OF PATHS AND NOT OF CONTENT, WHICH IS AN UNDECLARED LIMIT OF THE SAME CLASS ONE AXIS DOWN, FOUND BY REVIEW 3 AND DECLARED HERE. Everything this item does makes the entitlement domain and the validated set agree about WHICH PATHS are corpus members. NOTHING COMPARES THEIR BYTES: validate.py reads the WORKING TREE through disk_corpus, committed_blobs keys the INDEX blob, and no check asks whether they are the same object. DRIVEN AT 2f6cc25: commit a forged `{"schema": "nope", "verdict": "pass"}` over a tracked corpus path and leave the genuine bytes in the working tree UNSTAGED, so the index equals HEAD (not staged) and the path is on disk (not absent) and neither committed_blobs exclusion fires. `validate.py all` exits 0 with ZERO output lines; plain `reconcile-verdicts` appends a verdict.recorded declaring `"verdict": "pass"` and carrying verdict_blob 81fe14a7e5d150ec93346636727c0090b33c16a8, log md5 3ce08ca1f477 -> 8937421a420a and 862 -> 863 lines, and that blob holds the forgery while `git hash-object` of the working-tree file is 2699a63397c6d420, a different object no validator ever compared. IDENTICAL AT ffaab41 (exit 0, 0 lines, 1 appended, log md5 4b20b0fe19ec -> 01efc9b1adb9), so it is PRE-EXISTING and NOT a regression of this item, and outside the declared spelling-and-anchoring class. Also corrected: committed_blobs' argument `THE BYTES MUST BE THERE TO BE KEYED` proves only that the PATH is on disk, not that the bytes keyed were the bytes read. Named in the module's known-open list, in the spec's `What this item does NOT close`, and specified separately as WARP-0728 (DRAFT, unpromoted).
WARP-0727 is a STANDALONE enforcement spec (lane: standalone, depends_on: []), so this commit adds it to no plan's work list and moves no plan file.

THE FOOTPRINT IS WIDENED, NOT THE CHECK NARROWED. Routing the push guard's proof-manifest lookup through the owner puts scripts/warp-guard.sh and its eight further declared copies in this item's change set, and the shape gate named every one of them before the declaration was corrected.

TWO PUBLIC NAMES ARE RETIRED FROM events.py, CORPUS_PATHSPEC and CORPUS_PATHSPEC_FROM_TOP (as VERDICT_PATHSPEC and VERDICT_PATHSPEC_FROM_TOP), and the WARP-0725 AC4 binding that required the second name by TEXT moved with them in this same commit: it now requires corpus_pathspec and warp_root_for_log and requires the old name ABSENT, so nothing can quietly go on enumerating the repository root. A caller outside this repository that read either constant gets an AttributeError rather than a wrong answer, which is the direction that fails safe.

EVERY PATH THE OWNER RETURNS IS NOW RELATIVE TO THE WARP ROOT, where the domain used to answer relative to the top of the repository. In this repository the two are the same directory, so no recorded verdict_path changes. THE ONE PLACE THAT DISTINCTION IS NOT FOLLOWED THROUGH, DECLARED RATHER THAN CLAIMED CLOSED: the LEGACY resolver reads `<commit>:<path>` from an old-form event, which git resolves against the top of the repository, so a WARP root below the top would need a cwd-relative rev spelling. Old-form events exist only in this repository's own log, where the WARP root IS the top, and they were already unresolvable in a vendored copy for want of the commits; this round neither fixes nor worsens that.

THE PUSH GUARD'S OWN COMMENT WAS FALSE ABOUT python3 AND NOW DESCRIBES THE MEASURED BEHAVIOUR. Guard 2's proof-manifest lookup does fail closed on the corpus owner: driven three ways over a scratch clone whose gate record and manifest were made to name HEAD so the lookup is actually reached, the owner DELETED, the owner UNPARSEABLE and the manifest REMOVED each block at exit 2 with `No proof manifest found for HEAD`, while the unmodified state passes that guard and stops at the policy guard instead. python3 IS DIFFERENT: with no python3 on PATH the payload parse at the top of the script yields an EMPTY command, the push-and-merge match never fires, and the guard exits 0 having checked nothing - measured over a state that exits 2 with python3 present on the same trimmed PATH. That fail-open is byte-identical at ffaab41, so it is pre-existing and not this item's; it is a property of the payload parse rather than of the corpus lookup, and closing it needs a python3-independent way to read the hook JSON or a refusal when the parse itself could not run. The comment says exactly that instead of claiming a fail-closed the script does not have.

AN ARTIFACT THE WORKING TREE DOES NOT HOLD IS NO LONGER APPENDABLE, which is a change to what the projection will key and is declared as such. committed_blobs excludes it with the reason named, exactly as it already excluded a staged path and a non-regular index mode, and the argument is the same one: keying it writes a verdict.recorded for a review NOTHING HAS SEEN, and an append-only log cannot take that back. In this repository the two halves are equal (168 and 168), so no key changes and no recorded event moves. A repository using sparse-checkout to exclude the proof root will now see every artifact DEFERRED with the reason and a RED contract stage where it previously saw a green gate and an append.

THE RED DIRECTION COSTS ONE MORE GIT READ PER PATTERN, and the read is unrestricted on purpose. A pathspec would make it cheaper and would also make it share the surface it exists to check, so it asks git for everything at or below the WARP root and applies the ONE membership rule to the answer. THE `ABOUT 6 ms PER READ` FIGURE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED FROM THE MEASUREMENT: recounted this round at 2f6cc25, all FOUR reads together take 4 to 6 ms over the 2289 paths this WARP root tracks, so one read is about 1 ms. The cost that matters is applying the membership rule to the whole answer (24 ms for four patterns) and the under-proof-root test (14 ms), which is where the measured +43 ms per contract stage lives. A very large monorepo pays on the RULE at least as much as on the READ, and the honest bound is those numbers rather than a claim of free.

AN ADOPTER WHOSE CORPUS IS ON DISK BUT NOT YET COMMITTED NOW GETS ONE PRINTED LINE PER PATTERN saying so. It is a NAMED REPORT and not a failure, because git tracking nothing at all under the proof root is an author who has not committed yet rather than a broken enumeration; it is RED only when git reports something tracked there while the domain is empty. A repository with no proof root at all is byte-identically unaffected: divergence returns all-empty and the body scores 0, which is what makes deleting the early return safe as well as necessary.

WHAT ROUND 3 DID NOT CLOSE, DECLARED RATHER THAN LEFT: a corpus artifact COMMITTED IN ANOTHER REPOSITORY under the proof root is validated on disk while git reports it untracked from this root, so it lands in the legitimate `untracked` bucket and is not red unless the whole domain is empty. NOT ONLY A GITLINK, which is how this used to be written and reads as though a submodule were the trigger: a PLAIN NESTED REPOSITORY behaves identically, measured this round in both shapes over the same fixture - with the nested repo registered in the outer index (mode 160000) and with it registered nowhere at all, the artifact is validated, untracked, and neither a contradiction nor misfiled in both, the only difference being that the registered shape also puts the gitlink entry itself in tracked_under_proof. Distinguishing not-committed-yet from belongs-to-another-repository needs an ancestor test for a nested repository, and it is a separate item. The shapes this round measured (a symlinked proof root, a whitespace prefix, an index half with no working-tree half) are the ones the review named.
rollback: git revert the fix commit. The behavioural surface is four things: the corpus owner's signatures (root REQUIRED, no pathspec parameter, ONE root on divergence and misfiled), the anchoring itself (`:(top,literal)<warp root prefix>proof` in place of the two constants, and paths answered relative to that root), the entitlement anchor (warp_root_for_log in place of the log's nearest existing ancestor plus a top-anchored pathspec), and four corpus reads routed through the owner (three in policy_check.py, one in validate.py, one shell glob in warp-guard.sh). Everything else is prose corrections and two suite legs. All eight engine copies and nine guard copies are re-synced byte-identical, so a revert needs no manual fan-out.
